text.p: These are the leading stories in Sarajevo press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories nor does it vouch for their accuracy.

- There is no dispute between Bosnia's Moslem leaders and the international community as some political commentators speculated after presidency chairman, Alija Izetbegovic, criticised the implementation of the Dayton peace accord in a letter to major powers. It is rather a state of panic in the office of the High Representative because of its inability to carry out key provisions of the treaty, the paper says in a commentary.
- Director of World Bank office for Bosnia, Rory O'Sullivan, says no firm date has been set for international donors conference for Bosnian reconstruction.
- After the departure of the Social Democratic party, the opposition coalition Joint List which ran in the last elections does not exist any more, says opposition leader Sejfudin Tokic.

- Moslem-Croat federation enviroment minister, Ibrahim Morankic, says 41,114 apartments have been repaired so far and after privatisation begins, the price of an apartment per square meter will be between 110 and 120 German marks.

- Chairman of Bosnian presidency, Alija Izetbegovic, and Croatian President Franjo Tudjman are due to meet soon and will discuss the Dayton peace agreement, the trade deficit, dual citizenship and protection of property of Bosnian citizens who live in Croatia, ambassador to Croatia says.
- Religious leaders are close to organising an inter-religious council for Bosnia as agreed during Pope John Paul II's vist last month to Sarajevo. -- Sarajevo newsroom +387-71-663-86
